meta.description: NIA Senate hearing reconciliation workbook: published NEP detail, House GAB amounts, NIA original submission, edit acknowledgements and justifications, with a six-level hierarchy (program, sub-program, category, region, province, project). Title-embedded coordinates and chainage are parsed from the column-V fixed title when present (else the NEP-print label) using the shared gps-analysis and chainage builders; titles are never rewritten.
meta.join_note: One-to-one joins use exact (sub-program, canonical label, amount) then maximum-similarity matching inside exactly balanced (sub-program, amount) buckets; similarity is retained per row. Labels and amounts are never rewritten.

projects.category: Rehabilitation and Protection of Watershed Management
projects.label: Rehabilitation and Protection of Watershed Management
projects.submission_label: Rehabilitation and Protection of Watershed Management
projects.justification: On August 5, 2019, the National Irrigation Administration (NIA) and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) signed a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) to strengthen the sustainable management, protection, development, and rehabilitation of 143 watersheds supporting National Irrigation Systems (NIS) nationwide. Pursuant to DENR Memorandum Circular No. 2008-05, the agreement establishes the respective responsibilities of both agencies in preparing Integrated Watershed Management Plans (IWMPs), identifying priority watersheds for rehabilitation, securing environmental clearances, enforcing forestry laws, conducting research and information campaigns, and mobilizing funding resources. The partnership adopts an integrated watershed ecosystem management approach to ensure the long-term sustainability of irrigation systems while promoting environmental conservation and effective watershed management.

projects.justification: Considering that the entire Allay-Nangcalapan CIS is currently non-operational, it is necessary to prioritize its rehabilitation and restoration through the consolidation of available RESTO-CIS funds from two separate projects into a single project allocation. While the consolidated budget remains insufficient to fully restore the irrigation system, the proposed consolidation will enable the implementation of more substantial and strategically prioritized rehabilitation works, optimize the utilization of limited financial resources, and maximize the effectiveness and impact of the proposed interventions. This approach is intended to facilitate the progressive restoration of the system's operational functionality and ultimately restore irrigation services to its intended farmer-beneficiaries.
